overal.goal: Writes made through the stdio MCP server (`boof-runner mcp`) and through the CLI are not audited. The audit log (`audit/<date>.jsonl`) is written by the web server's audit middleware, so only REST and MCP-over-HTTP requests appear in it. A tool call over stdio runs `op.execute` in its own process as the local principal or a `--client`, and the hand-written and generated CLI commands write the stores directly; none of them leave an audit line. Record who did what for these paths too: one audit line per write operation (principal, operation, project, target, outcome, `via: stdio-mcp | cli`), written by the same code as the middleware and subject to the same `security.audit` settings. Fix it with the split's M3, when the operations run behind one shared executor.
overal.stack: TypeScript monorepo (Node 22 / Bun), Hono server, React + Vite UI, vitest

rules.do: Read README.md and docs/boof-runner.md for the intended behaviour before changing code.
Write a failing test first, then make it pass; keep the change focused on this goal.
Run `npm run typecheck && npx prettier --check . && npx vitest run && npm run build:server` before finishing.
rules.dont: Do not log request bodies, prompts or keys; the audit log records who, what, outcome and timing only.
Do not change public API or MCP shapes without updating docs and the OpenAPI document.
Do not commit secrets, data roots or build output.

versions.version: Found while planning the split's M0 (2026-11-02): with every operation on MCP and in the CLI, the writes that do not pass the web server leave no audit line; not started. Scheduled with M3.

Done early, on Heart core after M1: packages/shared/src/audit-log.ts (appendAuditLine, auditOperation, pruneAudit) is the one writer; the web middleware, the stdio MCP server (stdioAudit, via: stdio-mcp) and the generated CLI (via: cli) use it, one line per operation with principal, kind, action, project, outcome, ms and no arguments, under the same security.audit settings. Not done: the hand-written CLI commands (auth add, task move, plan sync, run, scan, project, remote, service) write no audit line; they need a design decision (they bypass op.execute and write stores directly).

tests.strategy: A stdio MCP tool call and a CLI write each append one audit line with the principal, the operation and the outcome, and none when security.audit.enabled is false; the line never holds a prompt or a key.
